name: Moringa (Moringa oleifera)
short: A review found no adverse effects reported in the few human studies of leaf preparations, but human data are sparse. A single case report links a leaf extract to a blood clot in the lungs.
text: A review of Moringa oleifera safety found that animal studies of water-based leaf extracts indicate a high degree of safety and that no adverse effects were reported in the human studies available, of which only five using powdered whole leaf had been published at the time. A later systematic review of the entire plant was more cautious: it stated that the plant is toxic at certain doses and that overuse can cause genotoxicity (the abstract does not say which plant part this concerns, or whether it comes from human, animal or laboratory studies), that little clinical trial data have been reported, and that toxicity needs further evaluation; most studies of its constituents were laboratory work only. A single case report describes a 63-year-old woman with obesity and type 2 diabetes who developed blood clots in both lungs after 5 months of taking a leaf extract supplement; the authors considered the supplement the likely trigger and called for cohort studies. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
